SHAKUNTALA VISHWAKARMA W/O SHRI DHIRENDRA VISHWAKARMA D/O SHRI RAMKARAN VISHWAKARMA R/O VILLAGE BHITARI, POLICE STATION RAMNAGAR, DISTRICT SATNA (MADHYA PRADESH) .....RESPONDENTS (SHRI GAJENDRA PARASHAR - PANEL LAWYER FOR RESPONDENT NO.1/STATE, NONE FOR RESPONDENT NO.2 EVEN IN THE SECOND ROUND ALTHOUGH REPRENSTED BY HER COUNSEL) This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following: ORDER This application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashment of FIR dated 23.11.2021 lodged by respondent No.2 in Crime No.1446/2021 at Police Station Kolgawan, District Satna for offence under Sections 498-A/34 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act. Dhirendra Vishwakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22438697/ 2 2. It is submitted by counsel for applicants that applicant No.1 is husband, applicant No.2 is mother-in-law (saas), applicant No.3 is elder brother-in-law (jaith), applicant No.4 is wife of elder brother-in-law (jaithani), applicant No.5 is sister-in-law (nanad), applicant No.6 is elder brother-in-law (jaith), applicant No.7 is sister-in-law (nanad) applicant No.8 is uncle-in-law (chacha sasur) of respondent No.2. Respondent No.2 lodged an FIR on 23.11.2021 on the allegations that she got married to applicant No.1 in the year 2015. For the first 3 years she was kept properly by her in-laws. She gave birth to two children but unfortunately both of them died. Thereafter, she could not conceive and on that ground her in-laws started harassing her physically and mentally and they also started making demand of Rs.50,000/-. On 17.07.2019 she has been turned out of her matrimonial house. The statement of respondent No.2 recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. is also in the same line as well as the statements of Smt. Shakuntala Vishwakarma/respondent No.2, Ravendra Vishwakarma/brother of respondent No.2, Ramkali Viswakarma/mother of respondent No.2 and Satendra Vishwakarma/brother of respondent No.2 are also in the same line and the allegations which have been mentioned in the FIR have been reiterated. 3. Challenging the registration of FIR as well as criminal proceedings, it is submitted by counsel for applicants that it is well established principle of law that if the allegations made against near and dear relatives of husband of the wife are vague, omnibus and general in nature, then relatives of husband of the wife should not be made to face the ordeal of criminal trial. In order to prosecute the near relatives of the husband of wife, the allegations should be clear and specific. In the present case, the allegations against all the applicants are vague, omnibus and general in nature. It appears that because respondent No.2 lost her children and thereafter, she could not conceive is the source of dispute and she has unnecessarily and falsely alleged the demand of dowry and harassment on account of non-fulfilment of said demand. 4. Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for State. 14. From a reading of the complaint, it cannot be held that even if the allegations are taken as proved no case is made out.
There are allegations against Respondent 2 and his parents for harassing the complainant which forced her to leave the matrimonial home.

The question whether the appellant has in fact been harassed and treated with cruelty is a matter of trial but at this stage, it cannot be said that no case is made out.
Thus, quashing of proceedings before the trial is not permissible.
